revision.text: Sadly, no. Hashes are made to be as random and entropic as possible; especially 512-bit hashes like we have here. Even while we know that, it doesn't help at all in breaking the hash because all of these hash types are assymetric, meaning that same characters do not have the same encrypted characters correlating to them. Also, hashes always have a fixed length, so words like 'ship' and an onion address have the same hash length. Lastly, this does ''not ''have to be an onion address. For all we know, it can be the content of the page, title of the page, or anything else relating to the page.

revision.text: I maybe phrased myself incorrectly. Even if the last 5 character are 'onion', which doesn't have to be so, as they may be referring to the content of the page, we don't know how many characters to subtract from the hash, because 5 characters in word != 5 characters in hash, due to its fixed size. There are simply too many variables to this, and I don't think cicada would require us to gather massive computational power to pass this stage of the puzzle. After all, if the hash is all we need, why did they make the rest of the Liber Primus? I am not saying the hash is unimportant, it's actually probably the key to solving the mystery of the LP, but I don't feel like bruteforcing is the way to go.
